explanation: Scan values into a HashSet and return true at the first failed insertion. A failed insertion means an earlier position already supplied the same value.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n values. Each of the n values is inserted or tested once with expected constant-time hashing.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. At most n distinct values are retained in the set.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Before each iteration the set contains exactly the earlier values. If add returns false, the current value equals an earlier one, proving a duplicate. If every insertion succeeds, all positions have different values, so false is correct.
walkthrough: For [8,1,5,8], the distinct set is {8,1,5}, with size 3 instead of 4. The second 8 introduces no new set entry, so return true.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays contain no duplicate.
A repeat need not be adjacent.
Negative values are ordinary set keys.
